# Standalone copy and upstream test port

The subject is rustc 1.99.0 (b940084d7, 2026-09-28). The supplied upstream test snapshot is rust-lang/rust tag 1.99.0, commit daa8d75bc715f77869fa06d80b6ea1a3fe52d38e. These are distinct provenance identifiers supplied with the audit.

All five core::net files are copied into `net-copy/src/net/`. `SHIMS.patch` records every changed line, except the added provenance header. `prepare.py` is the reproducible transformation. It removes compiler stability and diagnostic attributes, including inline variant-field attributes. `derive_const` becomes `derive`. `const impl` becomes `impl`, and the generic `[const] Into` bound becomes `Into`. The run-3 shims retain inherent `const fn` declarations. The schemata transformation makes guarded methods and their runtime callers non-const in the copy; every method needed by the unchanged upstream const tests remains const. [SCHEMATA.md](SCHEMATA.md) lists the separate builds required to preserve those tests. No feature flag or `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP` is used.

The root re-exports the standard `cmp`, `fmt`, `hash`, `mem`, `ops`, `error` and `str` modules. This preserves the original `crate::` import paths. The unstable MaybeUninit slice helpers are replaced by `slice::from_raw_parts` over the initialized byte prefix and a loop calling `MaybeUninit::write`. The original buffer length checks and initialized-length accounting remain.

Unstable net methods remain in the copy because the supplied upstream tests call them. Their public stable contract is outside the acceptance inventory. The upstream const tests are retained unchanged. Const trait implementations cannot be tested as const through this stable standalone crate; the inventory states this limitation.

All four supplied `library_coretests_tests_net_*.rs` files are ported. Only `use core::net::` changes to `use net_copy::net::`. A test-module wrapper is added. All 47 core tests run.

The supplied std socket test file contributes 11 value-type tests. Its imports change to `net_copy::net::*`. Four `ToSocketAddrs` tests and `bind_udp_socket_bad` are excluded. The supplied std IP test file contains one `ToSocketAddrs` test and is excluded. The supplied std net helper file supplies operating-system, DNS and socket helpers; it is not a value-type test suite and is not compiled. No DNS or socket operation runs. The exclusions preserve the offline and core::net scope. `SHIMS.patch` records the std socket exclusions verbatim. These exclusions constrain the meaning of “upstream tests stayed green”.

All 80 stable source doc examples also run against the copy. [DOC-TESTS.md](DOC-TESTS.md) and [DOC-TEST-REWRITES.patch](DOC-TEST-REWRITES.patch) record all 109 fenced blocks and every import rewrite. The 24 feature-gated examples retain their original attributes and are unported; stable compiler failures are recorded. Four non-Rust blocks and one should_panic example are excluded. Only import paths change in runnable examples. The full ported upstream suite therefore contains 138 tests, with these explicit exclusions.

Runtime mutations are compiled into one shared copy, selected by `NET_MUTANT` in each fresh test process. Const-dependent mutations use isolated copies and targets under `target/separate/`; the shared source is never patched for these builds. The generated switch and branches are reproduced by `schemata.py` and checked by `integrity.py`. Runtime assertion failures are required. Compiler failures do not count as detected behaviour. `evidence/gen/M*.patch` records the original literal mutation, and both upstream and proposed-test output remain available for every mutant. The upstream file and doc-test binaries both run even when the first fails. Exact test names and outcomes are compared with the preserved run-3 receipts. The outer runner reconstructs the shared schemata after failures without updating the immutable input pins.

`proposed.rs` contains the bounded assertion for every mutation. The feature `real-std` changes only the import to `std::net`. Both baselines must pass. Missing-test snippets use `core::net` and can be placed in the upstream net test modules.

Authored text files and text receipts carry the required provenance header. JSON records carry a provenance field. Binaries, Cargo target metadata and Python cache files are derived outputs. Copied source comments remain verbatim from upstream.

The applicability timestamp names the initial RFC and whole-stable-API scope declaration. Later serialization expands source items, trait members and compiler marker traits into separate rows. This expansion follows the stable signatures and does not select exclusions from test outcomes.
